figures.alt: Weather-resistant GFCI receptacle protected by a clear closed in-use cover on stucco
figures.caption: Exterior power needs protection from water and everyday use. Start by identifying the circuit, location, box condition, and the type of cover the finished outlet will need.
figures.before: When You Need a Permit in Jacksonville

figures.alt: Closed exterior electrical enclosure and weatherproof generator inlet on a Florida stucco wall
figures.caption: Outdoor electrical work belongs in a planned system. Equipment location, conduit routing, weather exposure, and available capacity should be considered together rather than adding an outlet in isolation.

figures.alt: Whole-house surge-protection module beside organized panel conductors
figures.caption: Jacksonville storms add a separate electrical risk. A qualified electrician can evaluate grounding, circuit protection, and surge strategy for the home, not only the new receptacle.
